# I-Ops

> Infrastructure that makes AI workers finish real tasks correctly: it determines what context a task
> needs, acquires what is missing under company permissions, governs consequential actions, and
> independently verifies the outcome. The worker that did the work does not get to declare it complete.

I-Ops Operations Intelligence LLC. Several of the layers are open source under Apache-2.0 and run
locally with no account.

## When to use this

Reach for I-Ops when the question is *what did the agent actually do*, not *what did it say*. The
tools below run locally, need no account and no network, and answer in one command.

- **An agent says it finished and you want to know what it skipped.** `uvx assurance audit` reads the
  session transcript and reports whether anything was tested after the last edit, whether a test run
  failed before a claim that it passed, where the run's budget went, and what it could not classify.
  Exit 1 means something to look at; exit 2 means it could not run.
- **Before an edit, to find out what it reaches.** `uvx assurance reach PATH` walks a code graph
  backwards and names what depends on the file, with the call site of each hop and how sure the graph
  is of it. It also says how far behind the code the graph is, so a stale answer is visible as one.
- **After an edit, to check it did what it said.** `uvx assurance reach --before A --after B --declared PATH`
  compares two graphs against paths declared before the run, and reports any dependency change outside
  them. It refuses rather than guesses when the two graphs cannot be compared.
- **Whether the person who asked may touch all of it.** `uvx assurance clearance PATH --declaration FILE --principal ID`
  joins what a change reaches to who owns it, read from CODEOWNERS. A file whose owner it cannot
  determine makes the answer NOT_ASKED rather than a pass.
- **Who wrote this project, and which AI helped.** `npx iops-rooms week` attributes commits to the
  person and the agent that co-authored them, from git history alone.
- **Natively, from an agent.** `assurance-mcp` is on the MCP registry and exposes these as read-only
  tools; the Claude Code plugin is in Anthropic's directory.

**When not to use it.** It does not make an agent's answers better, write code, or retrieve context
for a prompt. It is not a linter and not a test runner — it reads what your own tests and commands
already did. If nothing in your workflow produces a transcript, a run record or a code graph, there
is nothing here for it to read yet.

## Docs

- [For agents](https://i-ops.dev/agents.md): the full machine-readable summary — what I-Ops is, the
  tools and their install lines, what we do not claim, and every contact link.
- [For agents, as a page](https://i-ops.dev/agents/): the same content as HTML.
- [Open source](https://github.com/i-ops-hq): assurance and rooms. Source, issues, releases.

## Optional

- [Partner](https://i-ops.dev/partner/): for companies with a workflow to govern.
- [Early access](https://i-ops.dev/early-access/): the macOS app, in private testing.
